credit_conditions_survey_context.terms_and_conditions_summary: Banks reported significantly narrower spreads over funding costs, while maturities and collateral requirements tightened to different degrees. Maximum amounts and fees were broadly unchanged for companies overall.

interpretation: The inherited dollar-loan stock was concentrated in primary production and manufacturing; those two broad activities held 73.72% at 2026-Q2.
July gross dollar-credit operations were concentrated in legal persons outside the SME category used by the workbook. They received 74.59% of all cash-loan flows and 77.72% of single-name-note flows.

For other legal persons, the single-name-note flow combined a high weighted amount band with a short average term: USD 5-10 million, 150 days, and 53.49% below 90 days. This pattern is compatible with large, short-term corporate financing, but it does not identify the final use.
Funding is not the only observable bottleneck: the Q2 survey reported weak SME credit demand and expected tighter SME standards, although that survey is not specific to dollar credit.

The data clarify who and which sectors received credit before the new measure; they do not yet show who uses the new regulatory bucket or whether the proceeds become fixed investment, working capital, refinancing or another use.
caveats: Economic activity is the borrower's principal activity, not the destination of the loan.
The activity table does not cross activity, borrower size, loan line and final use in one observation.
Monthly operated amounts are gross flows, not outstanding stocks, unique borrowers or net credit creation.
'Other legal persons' is the workbook category complementary to SME legal persons; it must not be treated as perfectly identical to the survey's 'large companies' category.
The weighted amount band is an amount-weighted ordinal band code, not an average loan amount or a distribution of operations.
The credit-conditions survey records banks' perceptions and expectations across business credit; it is contextual evidence and not a measure of dollar-loan use.
All activity and survey observations precede the 2026-08-13 policy announcement, so post-policy outcomes remain unobserved.
